Re-enactors and visitors in historical costume at Grace Dieu Priory

The Friends of Grace Dieu Priory celebrated our 20th Anniversary Medieval Fayre with great success, welcoming hundreds of visitors to the conserved ruins under glorious 25°C weather.

### Highlights of the Day
- **Living History (1485 Camp):** Living history re-enactment groups, including the Friends of the Thomas Grey Household and the Ferrers Household, brought history alive with period armour, camp cooking, and crafts.
- **Archery & Drill:** Archers practised in the field opposite, followed by thrilling combat demonstrations and a traditional Mummers play (St George and the Dragon).
- **Music & Choirs:** The Sing It Happy Choir delighted audiences with acoustic choral performances inside the cloisters.
- **Community Market:** Local artisan stalls offered honey from Mount St Bernard's Abbey, handmade jewellery, preserves, woodcrafts, and Viking goods.
- **Refreshments:** Barista coffee, artisan pizza, burgers, and ice creams served behind the Tudor kitchen ruins.

Special thanks to our volunteer parking crew and car park marshals in Rusty Mary's field, Leicester University, Charnwood Geopark, and The Remet Company, Shepshed.

From Castles to Cloisters: The Remarkable Life of Roesia de Verdun
A fascinating lecture by guest historian Sarah Wolek exploring the life, legacy, and tomb of the priory's 13th-century founder.
St John the Baptist's Church, Belton

The de Verdun family were powerful medieval nobles whose influence spanned England, Ireland, and Wales. When no male heir survived to inherit the family’s vast estates, Roesia de Verdun took control and ensured the dynasty’s fortunes continued.

This special talk by historian Sarah Wolek took place beside Roesia’s tomb in St John the Baptist's Church, Belton. The presentation illuminated what the iconography of her tomb reveals about her life and achievements, earning praise from King Henry III for accomplishing what none of her forefathers could.

800-Year-Old Medieval Priory Wall Uncovered by Volunteer Clearance
Clearing dense overgrowth and tidying paths with Charnwood Forest Geopark volunteers has revealed previously hidden sections of the 800-year-old Augustinian wall.
Exposed ancient medieval priory wall following vegetation clearance

We would like to extend our immense gratitude to our friends and volunteers at **Charnwood Forest Geopark** for their outstanding hands-on support.

During joint conservation working parties focused on tidying visitor footpaths and clearing invasive brambles, volunteers successfully exposed an intact section of the priory's original 800-year-old medieval wall.

This discovery provides fresh insight into the monastic boundary architecture and will form a key focal point for upcoming educational guided walks.

Saving Grace Dieu Priory: An Appeal to the Local Community
Published in the Belton Maypole magazine: tracing 30 years from ivy-covered ruins in 1995 to public opening, and issuing a vital appeal for new volunteer blood.

*The following article appeared in the October 2025 edition of the Belton Maypole magazine:*

In 1995 Grace Dieu Priory was a pile of stone covered in ivy. A dedicated group of local residents came together to save what was left, and the **Grace Dieu Priory Charitable Trust** company was born. The Trust now owns the Priory and Rusty Mary's field.

Between 1996 and 2006, extensive conservation work was carried out and, after overcoming many setbacks, the Priory was opened free of charge to the public. The **Friends of Grace Dieu Priory** was formed and registered as a Charity (No. 1117921) to manage day-to-day tasks. Over the last 20 years, the Priory has hosted thousands of visitors at events organised solely by volunteers, with no direct funding from any statutory body.

### An Urgent Appeal for Volunteers
The founding committee is aging and struggling to maintain the necessary level of activity. The Priory is financially sound and we hope to build a new bridge from Rusty Mary's field into the Priory.

We are not going to lock the gates in the near future, but unless we can recruit new help, that risk looms.

If you have office and administrative skills, digital know-how, or a bit of muscle to help put up gazebos and marshal parking at events, please consider becoming a Friend. We would love to welcome more younger members. You would be made very welcome!

Grace Dieu Priory Sold to Charitable Trust: Permanent Ownership Secured
After two years of detailed negotiations with private landowners, the Grace Dieu Priory Trust has acquired the freehold ownership of the priory ruins and Rusty Mary's field.
BBC News report headline: Grace Dieu Priory Sold to Trust

In November 2024, our parent organisation, **The Grace Dieu Priory Trust**, officially acquired the freehold of the entire site after two years of negotiations with private landowners.

Having previously cared for the monument as tenants, freehold ownership now provides long-term certainty and substantial flexibility to execute ambitious conservation work.

Planned initiatives include:
- Scheduled archaeological excavations across previously unexplored ground.
- Capital works to build a dedicated footbridge linking Rusty Mary's field to the priory precinct.
- Continued consolidation and restoration of delicate medieval stonework.

20th Anniversary Medieval Fayre: A Resounding Community Success
Reflecting on our glorious 20th anniversary community celebration featuring 1485 living history camps, archery drills, Sing It Happy choir, and local artisan markets.
Re-enactors and visitors in historical costume in the priory cloisters

The Friends of Grace Dieu Priory would like to extend our warmest thanks to everyone who attended our 20th Anniversary Medieval Fayre, which proved to be a resounding success!

### A Sunlit Day of Pageantry
After a very hot spell, the 28th of June 2026 was forecast to be a pleasant **25°C**—just right for the Medieval Fayre. Having looked after the ancient monument for 20 years, we wanted to celebrate this milestone with an event the entire community could share free of charge. After months of preparation, during which the final two setup days saw temperatures soaring over **30°C**, pitch markings for traders and car parking in Rusty Mary's field were ready to welcome our guests.

At 7:00 AM, the gates opened and our first living history reenactment groups and market traders began to arrive. Before our eyes, the priory was transformed into a 1485 medieval encampment with period armouries, camp cooking, and traditional woodcrafts, while arrows took flight in the practice drills across the meadow.

### Choirs, Combat & Community Spirit
By 10:30 AM, the ruins were bustling with hundreds of visitors trying on replica medieval helmets, learning squire combat drills, and trying wood-turning on period pole-lathes. The **Sing It Happy Choir** delighted audiences with acoustic choral harmony inside the ruined cloisters. Refreshments were served behind the Tudor kitchen, and families gathered to watch the traditional Mummers play as St George vanquished the dragon.

### Sincere Thanks to Our Volunteers
Our volunteer car park marshals did a sterling job guiding visitors safely into spaces in Rusty Mary’s field throughout the day. We would like to thank:
- The fabulous reenactment households: **The Friends of the Thomas Grey Household** and **The Ferrers Household**.
- Our partners at **Charnwood Forest Geopark** and their hardworking volunteer crew.
- The **University of Leicester** archaeology team and **The Remet Company, Shepshed**.
- All volunteer marshals and gate crew who made the day run seamlessly.

Most of all, thank you to our community for coming along, supporting the event, and leaving the monument ruins so clean and tidy.

Cover of Dame Petronella's Account Book 1414-1418
Cheques payable to Grace Dieu Priory Trust please. Obtainable solely from Ann Petty.

*Please note: The price of Dame Petronella's 1414-1418 Account Book has been reduced to **£15.00 + £4.00 p&p**.*

This rare historical volume preserves the working drafts that lay behind the formal monastic accounts—documents that typically perished over time. Later annotated with headings of classic manorial accounts, the text details both priory income (principally rents from nearby settlements) and daily expenditures.

Purchases recorded include meat, fish, household foodstuffs, masonry building works, agricultural wages, and servants' stipends. It provides an extraordinary window into early 15th-century English social, economic, and monastic life.

### Scholarly Apparatus
- **Preface:** Professor Christopher Dyer (University of Leicester).
- **Introduction:** 29-page historical study by trustee Kenneth Hillier.
- **Transcription & Translation:** Rendered from medieval Latin by genealogist Dominic Johnson.
- **Editorial Conventions:** Notes on the Latinity of the priory clerks by the late Lesley Boatwright.
- Complete glossary of medieval English and Latin terminology, comprehensive indices of persons, places, and subjects, and calendar of Saints' Days and holy festivals.

Cheques payable to Grace Dieu Priory Trust. Proceeds split between Loughborough Naturalists' Club and Friends of Grace Dieu Priory.

A beautifully produced volume authored by renowned regional naturalists Steve Woodward and Helen Ikin of the **Loughborough Naturalists' Club**.

This comprehensive study documents the flora, fauna, lichens, and unique geological formations found within the Grace Dieu Priory estate, the Grace Dieu brook, and the surrounding Charnwood ancient woodlands.

Proceeds from the sale of this book directly support both The Loughborough Naturalists' Club and The Friends of Grace Dieu Priory.
